result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (3 tests, including a new one) pass, and I verified the two negative cases by temporarily applying the misspellings across `resources/js/` and confirming typecheck fails, then reverting.

I made the sign-up route declare its contract instead of keeping the shape only in the page. In `routes/auth.ts:14` the `register.store` route is now registered with the route-contract form — `guest.post('/register', { name: 'register.store', body: RegisterSchema }, [RegisterController, 'store'])` — matching how `posts.store`/`posts.update` are already registered in `routes/web.ts`; for controller-action handlers the contract is metadata only, so `RegisterController.store()` still does the validating and the rules, path, route name and 422 behaviour are untouched. Re-running `bun run codegen` made `.guren/api-client.gen.ts:88` emit `body: { name: string; email: string; password: string; passwordConfirmation: string }` for `register.store`, and `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` now derives everything from that: `type RegisterFormData = ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']`, the `errors` prop typed as `ValidationErrors<keyof RegisterFormData & string>` (keeping the general `message` slot), and submission via `form.post(route('register.store'))` instead of the hard-coded `/register`. So a misspelled field in the initial values, in `form.data`/`form.setData`, or in an error read fails typecheck against the server-side schema, and a misspelled route name fails against the generated manifest. I also added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts`, which primes CSRF and asserts a mismatched confirmation still returns 422 with `errors.passwordConfirmation`.
